newsitem.title: UK: UK to restrict BBC TV licence fee rises over 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: UK to restrict BBC TV licence fee rises over 5 yrs.

text.p: The government has set a structure for changes in the BBC television licence fee providing for an average rise of 0.08 percent below the rise in retail prices over the next five years, National Heritage Secretary Virginia Bottomley said on Wednesday.

Bottomley said in a parliamentary written answer that the fee for 1997/8 would be allowed to rise in line with retail price inflation from its present 89.50 stg for a colour television and 30 stg for a black and white one.
In the subsequent four years, the rises would be RPI plus three percent, RPI plus 0.5 percent, RPI minus one percent and RPI minus 2.5 percent, she added.

"This equates to a change in the level of the licence fee over the five year period of RPI minus 0.08 pct," she said. "The non-uniform pattern of annual changes reflects the need for expenditure on new digital services in the early years."

"This will be offset in 1997/98 by receipts from the sale of the BBC's transmission system, and in later years by increased efficiency savings and commercial income." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
